PetroVietnam Technical Services Corp Reports Steady Quarterly Growth in UAE Operations

PetroVietnam Technical Services Corp, a leading provider in the oil and gas services and equipment sector, has posted stable financial results for its operations in the United Arab Emirates in the most recent quarter, reflecting continued demand and robust project execution in the region.

The company reported a 4.2% year-on-year increase in quarterly revenue, reaching AED 312 million, driven by ongoing contracts in offshore maintenance and engineering services. Net profit for the quarter stood at AED 41 million, up from AED 39 million in the same period last year. Margins remained healthy, aided by operational efficiencies and cost management initiatives implemented over the past year.

Nguyen Minh Tuan, Regional Director for the Middle East at PetroVietnam Technical Services Corp, attributed the results to “strong client relationships and our commitment to delivering technical excellence across all project phases.” He added, “Our teams in Abu Dhabi and Sharjah have maintained high safety and performance standards, ensuring uninterrupted service to our key partners.”

The company’s order backlog in the UAE climbed to AED 1.2 billion as of the end of the quarter, supported by recent contract extensions with major upstream operators and a new multi-year agreement with Emirate Energy Solutions, a local oilfield services provider. PetroVietnam Technical Services Corp has also expanded its workforce by 7% this quarter, responding to increased activity on offshore brownfield upgrade projects.

Industry analysts noted the steady growth was consistent with broader trends in the UAE’s oilfield services market, which has benefited from stable crude prices and sustained investment in infrastructure. “PetroVietnam Technical Services Corp continues to show resilience and adaptability as clients seek reliable partners for complex engineering and maintenance tasks,” said Hassan Al Rahmani, a senior analyst at Gulf Energy Insights.

The UAE’s Oil & Gas Services and Equipment Association welcomed the quarterly results, describing them as “a positive indicator of sector stability and ongoing investment in technical capacity.” The association cited a recent uptick in demand for specialized services, including subsea inspection and asset integrity management.

Looking ahead, Nguyen said the company will focus on digitalization and workforce training, aiming to enhance project delivery and support the UAE’s long-term energy goals. No significant disruptions or operational issues were reported during the period.
